_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive E: Mahabharata birth-myths and framing narratives (Ganguli 1883-96, public domain).

title.en: Janamejaya's Snake Sacrifice and the Rescue by Astika
title.zh: 闍那彌覺耶的蛇祭與阿悉底迦之救

region.en: Takshashila / Taxila (traditional site of the rite)
region.zh: 怛叉始羅（祭祀傳統聖地）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Astika Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Astika section

summary.en: King Parikshit dies of the serpent-king Takshaka's bite; his son Janamejaya holds a sacrificial fire so powerful that all serpents of the world are dragged into it to burn. The young brahmin Astika, son of a serpent mother, stops the holocaust with a request - and the serpents' race is saved, which is why the Mahabharata itself is being recited at all.
summary.zh: 帕里格希王死於蛇王多剎迦之咬；其子闍那彌覺耶設祭火之力足以將世間一切蛇拖入焚燬。年輕婆羅門阿悉底迦，蛇母之子，以一請求止此浩劫——蛇族得救；這也是《摩訶婆羅多》本身被誦出的緣由。

passages.text: King Parikshit, cursed by a seer's son, was told he would die in seven days by the bite of Takshaka the serpent-king; he built a tower, sealed it - and Takshaka came disguised, and the king died as foretold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: His son Janamejaya vowed revenge: a snake-sacrifice was raised whose fire drew the serpents of the whole earth into its blaze, kingdom by kingdom, name by name, until even Takshaka was pulled toward the flames.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then Astika, a boy brahmin of a mixed birth - his father a seer, his mother a serpent-woman - praised the king and begged a boon: let the sacrifice stop while my kinsmen live. The king granted it; the serpents were released, the feud ended - and the story the world now reads was told first at that sacrifice, by its own survivor.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Garuda Steals the Amrita for His Mother's Freedom
title.zh: 金翅鳥為母贖身而奪甘露

region.en: Ocean of amrita (symbolic pin at Varanasi ghats)
region.zh: 甘露之海（象徵性定位於瓦拉納西河壇）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Astika Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the birth of Garuda

summary.en: The sisters Vinata and Kadru, wives of Kashyapa, made a fatal wager about the horses of the sun; Kadru's serpent sons enslaved Vinata and her egg-son. The egg hatched into Garuda, of impossible fire and wings; he won his mother's freedom by bringing the gods' amrita from the churning-ocean stronghold - fighting the gods, stealing the nectar, and honoring Vishnu with a covenant: he became the god's own carrier.
summary.zh: 迦葉波之二妻毗娜達與迦德魯就日馬之事立致命之賭；迦德魯的蛇子們奴役了毗娜達及其卵中之子。卵孵化為火翼無雙的金翅鳥；他以從攪乳海要塞奪來的諸神甘露換取母親的自由——戰諸神、竊神露，並與毘濕奴立約：他成為神之座騎。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Garuda imagery across Asia); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The wager: Kadru said the sun's white horses had black tails; Vinata swore they were pure white. Kadru's serpent-sons made her right by clinging to the tails; the loser became the winner's slave, mother and egg.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The egg broke open with fire: Garuda, huge-winged, feathered like flame, heard his mother's condition and flew to the gods' stronghold to fetch the amrita - the price the serpents set for Vinata's freedom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: He scattered the gods with a storm of wings, took the nectar, and Vishnu, impressed, made a covenant: Garuda became his carrier, and his own body immortal without the drink; the amrita was set out as ransom, the serpents licked it from the grass, and their tongues split forever - the covenant that made Garuda the enemy and liberator of serpents both.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Ganga's Sons and Bhishma's Eight Births
title.zh: 恆河之子與毗濕摩的八次誕生

region.en: Pratapa of the Ganges at Prayag (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 般耶伽恆河畔（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Ganga and Shantanu

summary.en: King Shantanu met a beautiful woman who married him on one condition: never ask what she did with their children. Seven sons were born and drowned one by one. The eighth was kept - Devavrata, the future Bhishma - and the river-bride, revealed as Ganga herself, left him with the story of eight gods imprisoned on earth and her task of releasing them.
summary.zh: 王商檀奴遇絕色女子，其嫁他有唯一條件：永不問她如何處置孩子。七子相繼誕生又相繼被溺。第八子被留下——婆德伐羅陀，未來的毗濕摩——而那位河畔新娘，現身為恆河本尊，帶著八位囚於人間之神與她釋放之任的故事離去。

passages.text: The woman of the river promised herself to Shantanu if he asked no questions: never whatever I do with our children, with or against thy will - and he, enamored, agreed; the sons born of her were drowned at birth, one after another, and the king could not speak.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The eighth birth: when Ganga raised the child to drown him, Shantanu cried out at last - and she stopped, gave him the boy Devavrata, and told the secret: the eight Vasus, gods of light, had been cursed into human birth, and she had been their ferry; seven she had released to heaven at once.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Devavrata stayed as Shantanu's heir - the one Vasu whose curse ran its longest course - and the hero's later terrible vow of celibacy (bhishana, the 'terrible', hence Bhishma) completes the freight of the river's bargain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Satyavati the Fisher-Girl and Vyasa the Island-Born
title.zh: 漁家女莎蒂亞瓦蒂與生於島上的毗耶娑

region.zh: 亞穆納河渡口（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Sambhava section

summary.en: The girl Satyavati, ferrying travelers across the Yamuna smelling of fish, met the seer Parashara; he offered her a boon - she chose that her fish-smell become fragrance, her maidenhood return, and her river-mist conceal their union on an island. Their son was Vyasa, the compiler of the Mahabharata itself - the epic written by its own love-child.
summary.zh: 魚味少女莎蒂亞瓦蒂渡旅人於亞穆納河，遇仙人婆羅沙羅；他允其一恩——她選擇魚味化香、處子復得、河霧蔽於島上的結合。其子即毗耶娑，《摩訶婆羅多》的編纂者——史詩由其自身的愛之子寫成。

passages.text: The ferry-girl ruled the river-crossing with a will; the seer Parashara, crossing, desired her; she refused him at first, and he offered boons until she bargained: my fish-smell to sweetness, my virginity restored, and a mist to hide us from the two banks.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: On the island in the mist a child was conceived and born within the hour, dark, wise, island-born - Dvaipayana, Vyasa - who went at once to do austerities, promising his mother to come whenever she thought of him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The daughter of the fisher-king rose by that fortune to be the grandmother of both armies - and Vyasa's promise kept: it is he who comes when the dynasty calls, to father its heirs and write its epic.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Pandu's Curse in the Deer Forest

region.en: Shatasringa hermitage (symbolic pin in Himalayan foothills)
region.zh: 百峰仙人道場（象徵性定位於喜馬拉雅山麓）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Sambhava section

summary.en: King Pandu, on a hunt, shot a stag mid-union with its doe - and the stag was a seer. Dying, he cursed Pandu: union with a woman shall be death for him. Pandu renounced the throne to his blind brother and lived in the forest; his sons - the Pandavas - were born not of him but of the gods his wives invoked: the theology of the five heroes' divine fathers.
summary.zh: 王般度狩獵時射中一頭正與牝鹿交合的雄鹿——而牠是仙人。垂死的詛咒降於般度：與女子交合即死。般度讓位於盲眼的弟弟，居於林中；其子——般度五子——非其親生，而是諸神經由其妻的召喚而生：五英雄神性之父的神學。

passages.text: Pandu's arrow found the stag in the forest clearing - and the dying creature stood up as a sage and delivered the curse: the same arrow shall find thee in the moment of thy joy; know death in the embrace.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Pandu gave up the kingdom, the pleasures and the palace, and went to the Himalayan foothills with his two wives; the throne passed to the blind Dhritarashtra and the age's tragedy was set in motion by a hunter's mistake.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: In the forest the wives were given mantras: Kunti bore three sons of gods she invoked - Yudhishthira of Dharma, Bhima of the Wind, Arjuna of Indra - and Madri two of the Ashvins; the Pandavas are therefore gods' sons on a cursed father's name, the epic's own theology of legitimacy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Amba's Terrible Birth: The Story of Shikhandin
title.zh: 安巴的可怕轉生：希甘丁的故事

region.zh: 迦屍與俱盧之野（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Amba Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the story of Amba

summary.en: At the svayamvara of the three Kashi princesses, Bhishma carried them off for his brother's marriage-bed; Amba, already pledged to another, was returned by the rules of honor - but her bridegroom refused her, ruined. She turned for redress to Bhishma himself, then to Shiva: born again as Shikhandin, she finally faced the old man on the battlefield he had sworn not to fight.
summary.zh: 在迦屍三公主的自擇婚禮上，毗濕摩為其弟之婚床擄走三女；安巴已許他人，依榮譽之規則被送回——但她的新郎因她受辱而拒娶。她轉而向毗濕摩討公道，繼而向濕婆：轉生為希甘丁後，她終於在老人誓不與戰的戰場上與他對面。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; gendered readings contested; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Bhishma, sent to win brides for his brother, took the three princesses of Kashi by force of arms from their svayamvara - a deed of honor in his own code, and an abduction in everyone else's.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Amba section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Amba's plea: she had already chosen a husband. Bhishma honored her word and sent her back - and the bridegroom, hearing she had dwelt in another man's chariot, refused her; ruined twice over, she turned her whole life into a single accusation.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Amba section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Her austerities were answered by Shiva with the promise of rebirth to destroy Bhishma - born again as Shikhandin, a warrior whose past Bhishma knew; on the tenth day of the great war, Arjuna's arrows passed over Shikhandin's body to reach Bhishma, who would not raise his bow against the one he wronged - the debt collected at last.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva and Bhishma Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Bhishma's Terrible Vow at the Fisherman's Ford
title.zh: 毗濕摩於漁人渡口的可怕誓言

region.zh: 恆河渡口，俱盧之野一帶（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Bhishma's vow

summary.en: Shantanu loved Satyavati the ferry-girl; her father demanded that her sons inherit. Devavrata, the river's own son and heir, made the vow that bought her: he renounced the throne, and then - for the girl's sons might still fear his descendants - renounced children altogether. The gods rained flowers on a vow so terrible it named him: Bhishma.
summary.zh: 商檀奴愛上渡舟女莎蒂亞瓦蒂；其父要求她之子繼承王位。河神之子、法定繼承人婆德伐羅陀立誓買下她：放棄王位，繼而——因女孩之子或仍懼其後裔——放棄後嗣。諸神對如此可怕的誓言降下花雨，此誓亦為他命名：毗濕摩（『可怕者』）。

passages.text: The fisherman's price for his daughter was succession: her sons shall reign. Devavrata answered by giving up the throne his birth gave him - and, pressed further, by giving up posterity itself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The vow was spoken at the ford: I shall never marry, never touch a woman, and my life shall end only when the gods appoint - so strong that heaven opened and flowers fell, and the witnesses named him Bhishma, the terrible.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The whole war is downstream of that vow: the childless Bhishma as regent, the succession crisis of his vow's collateral, and the old man on the arrows-bed at Kurukshetra who taught dharma from the wreck of the kingdom his own word had helped to make.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Bhima and Hidimba: The Rakshasa Bride
title.zh: 怖軍與訶底撥：羅剎之妻

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Hidimva and Ghatotkacha

summary.en: Exiled in the forest, the Pandavas camped where the rakshasa Hidimba and his sister hunted men. The sister, Hidimbi, saw Bhima and chose him; her brother attacked, and Bhima's mace decided it. From the marriage of princess and rakshasa came Ghatotkacha, the pot-born giant, his head shaped like a pot, who would die at Kurukshetra saving Arjuna.
summary.zh: 流亡林中的般度五子在羅剎訶底撥與其妹的獵人之地紮營。妹妹訶底毗見怖軍而屬意之；其兄來攻，怖軍之杵定勝負。公主與羅剎之婚誕生了罐首巨人無底缽迦，他將在俱盧之野為救阿周那而死。

passages.text: Hidimbi, sent by her man-eating brother to scout the sleepers, found Bhima awake and beautiful - and warned him instead: your brothers and Draupadi are in danger; my brother comes to eat them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The duel that followed was giant against giant: Bhima's strength held through the night, and Hidimba fell; the rakshasa woman, her protector dead, claimed the hero by her brother's own dying law - a marriage of the strong.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Yudhishthira's terms were exile-tight: one son, then they part. Ghatotkacha was born pot-headed, gigantic, devoted to his father's family; he served the Pandavas their whole exile and, at Kurukshetra, flew into Karna's spear - a son spent to save a father's brother.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva and Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Arjuna and Ulupi, the Naga Princess

region.en: Ganges, Manipur route (symbolic pin at Haridwar)
region.zh: 恆河，曼尼普爾之路（象徵性定位於赫里德瓦爾）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Arjuna's wanderings

summary.en: Wandering penance-bound after a transgression, Arjuna bathed in the Ganges at night - and was seized by the naga princess Ulupi, who drew him down to the serpent city, married him, and gave him the boon his celibacy needed: victory over every water-being. Their son Iravan would die a hero's death at Kurukshetra.
summary.zh: 因觸戒而流浪贖罪中的阿周那夜浴恆河——被龍女鄔樓毗攫住，帶入蛇城，與之成婚，並賜予其苦行生活所需之恩：戰勝一切水族。其子伊拉萬將於俱盧之野戰死，死如英雄。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Iravan/Koothandavar cult in Tamil country); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Arjuna's penance-law forbade the bed of any woman; at the night-bath the naga princess Ulupi took him at the wrists and drew him, unresisting, into the river's deep - to the city of the serpents, where she offered her love with the law's own loophole.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The loophole: the vow bound him against desire, not against the water's gift - and Ulupi's marriage-bed counted as neither; she bore him Iravan, and gave him the practical blessing that his river-life needed: no water-creature shall overcome thee.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: He returned by morning to his brothers as if nothing had happened; the son he left behind grew into a self-sacrificing warrior of the war, and in the Tamil south his cult continues in rituals of self-offering to this day.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.zh: 阿周那與曼尼普爾的希甘提耶

region.zh: 曼尼普爾（象徵性定位，東部邊地）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Arjuna's wanderings

summary.en: The third of Arjuna's exile-marriages: at the river-city of Manipur the warrior-princess Chitrangada approached him herself and asked to be his wife. He stayed a season; she bore him Babhruvahana, who as a boy at Kurukshetra would kill his own father - and be forgiven, in the epic's strangest family accounting.
summary.zh: 阿周那流亡中的第三次婚姻：在河城曼尼普爾，女戰士希甘提耶親自來求嫁。他居留一季；她為他生子巴布魯婆訶那，後者在俱盧之野以童子之身親手弒父——並被饒恕，於史詩最奇異的家庭清算之中。

passages.text: Chitrangada, only daughter of the Manipur king, had been raised as his heir and warrior; hearing of Arjuna's penance-wanderings, she came to the hermitage herself, dressed plainly, and asked - not for a beauty's marriage but a warrior's.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Arjuna stayed a season by the river-city; their son Babhruvahana was sent to be raised as his mother's heir, and Manipur passed to the Pandavas' line without a war.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The epic's coda: years later at Kurukshetra, the Ashvamedha horse reached Manipur, and the boy-king Babhruvahana fought the rider - his father - and felled him; Ulupi's serpent-charm revived Arjuna, and the son knelt to a father restored - a family puzzle the epic refuses to judge.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
